Newcomer John Llewellin, he won the handicap at Enfield, with a sub 56 for 7 in his 1st Open., Neil Foster, although at College in Liverpool has managed trips back for races as well as various meetings up North, and Michael Feighan another with great prospects have all been well up in the finishing orders..

Coming up through in the longer events and behind Stephen Marshall in the Barking was Michael Feighan breaking the cadets course record, he also had the audacity to finish 3rd Belgrave man in the club 20m run.
Results; S.Marshall 4:50.11; 22.R.Day 6:06.42; In the Cadets race held at the same time, M.Feighan won with a new record of approximately 5hr.35.
Which brings me to the 'youngsters', Neil Foster, 3rd in the SCAAA 10kms and 2nd in the Club 10m, Michael Feighan (likened in style to Stan Vickers, but not quite the speed yet) and Murray Day.

Winner of the 'A' section was Amos Seddon who in 1966 (18 years before) won the 'B' section in the same event. 'A': 7.J.Newnham 11946m; 'B': 5.D.Fotheringham 11310m; 14.R.Middleton 10733; 18.J.Bromley 10484m; 'C': 1.M.Feighan 11430m.

On June 30th Michael Feighan won an Open 5Km at Brighton 24:16.5 with Eric Crutcher 2nd, 24:49.5; and John Llewellyn 3rd 105.44 with John Newnham 5th - 109.46 in the Woodham Ferrers half marathon walk.
Belgrave just managed to get four round, but that was it. 1.L.Morton (Sheff) 4:19.09; 19.C.Lawton 5:07.57; 20.M.Feighan 5:08.05; 34.J.Dunsford 5:41.23; 40.J.Morris 5:59.04.
At Briantspuddle (Dorset) on Sunday in the Open 7 miles, Carl Lawton was 4th 54.25; 10th M.Feighan 57.45 and 11th John Newnham 57.49 to give Belgrave second behind Dawlish.
Backing up were Lawton, Hall and Michael Feighan making his last appearance for us before leaving for the United States to take up basket making.
